labels.notes_for_labeler: CONFIRMED (real run). Mechanical abstention did NOT reproduce (blockquote '>' prefix handled fine by the tolerant locator). Validator DID reject, but on inspection this looks like a DEFENSIBLE rejection, not an FPO #12-style miscalibration: the new_code only stores `self.jitter = jitter`, it never shows jitter actually being applied to retry timing. The corrector's proposed text ('If jitter is set to True, randomization is applied between attempts') asserts a behavior that isn't actually visible in the shown code snippet -- the same 'delegated/unprovable behavior' pattern as case 002, not the 'accurate but non-narrating' pattern of cases 005/007/028/029. Locking validator_status=rejected_accuracy as the gold label, distinct in kind from the FPO #12 cases despite the surface-level similarity (a rejection under rejected_accuracy on a change that looks additive).
